title: Tidy output from odin2, dust2 and monty
text: stochastic SIR model also tracks daily incidence, can compared case data: Run 30 particles tidy result. tidy_simulation() needs system times well output, array record either:  summarise_trajectories() collapses particles (draws chains, present) ribbon plot:
code: sir <- odin({   update(S) <- S - n_SI   update(I) <- I + n_SI - n_IR   update(R) <- R + n_IR   update(incidence) <- incidence + n_SI   p_SI <- 1 - exp(-beta * I / N * dt)   p_IR <- 1 - exp(-gamma * dt)   n_SI <- Binomial(S, p_SI)   n_IR <- Binomial(I, p_IR)   initial(S) <- N - I0   initial(I) <- I0   initial(R) <- 0   initial(incidence, zero_every = 1) <- 0   N <- parameter(1000)   I0 <- parameter(10)   beta <- parameter(0.4)   gamma <- parameter(0.1)   cases <- data()   cases ~ Poisson(incidence) }, quiet = TRUE) sys <- dust_system_create(sir, list(), n_particles = 30, dt = 0.25) dust_system_set_state_initial(sys) t <- 0:60 y <- dust_system_simulate(sys, t) dim(y) #> [1]  4 30 61  sim <- tidy_simulation(y, sys, t) sim #> # A tibble: 7,320 × 4 #>    particle  time variable  value #>       <int> <int> <chr>     <dbl> #>  1        1     0 S           990 #>  2        1     0 I            10 #>  3        1     0 R             0 #>  4        1     0 incidence     0 #>  5        2     0 S           990 #>  6        2     0 I            10 #>  7        2     0 R             0 #>  8        2     0 incidence     0 #>  9        3     0 S           990 #> 10        3     0 I            10 #> # ℹ 7,310 more rows ggplot(sim, aes(time, value, group = particle)) +   geom_line(alpha = 0.3) +   facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_y") ggplot(summarise_trajectories(sim), aes(time)) +   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.3) +   geom_line(aes(y = median)) +   facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_y")

title: Tidy output from odin2, dust2 and monty
text: Variables dimensions get one index column per dimension. dims names columns labels turns index labelled factor:
code: sir_age <- odin({   update(S[]) <- S[i] - n_SI[i]   update(I[]) <- I[i] + n_SI[i] - n_IR[i]   update(R[]) <- R[i] + n_IR[i]   p_SI <- 1 - exp(-beta * sum(I) / sum(N) * dt)   p_IR <- 1 - exp(-gamma * dt)   n_SI[] <- Binomial(S[i], p_SI)   n_IR[] <- Binomial(I[i], p_IR)   initial(S[]) <- N[i] - 5   initial(I[]) <- 5   initial(R[]) <- 0   N <- parameter()   beta <- parameter(0.4)   gamma <- parameter(0.1)   n_age <- parameter(2)   dim(S, I, R, n_SI, n_IR, N) <- n_age }, quiet = TRUE)  sys <- dust_system_create(sir_age, list(N = c(300, 700)), n_particles = 10) dust_system_set_state_initial(sys) y <- dust_system_simulate(sys, t)  sim_age <- tidy_simulation(y, sys, t, dims = "age",                            labels = list(age = c("children", "adults"))) sim_age #> # A tibble: 3,660 × 5 #>    particle  time variable age      value #>       <int> <int> <chr>    <fct>    <dbl> #>  1        1     0 S        children   295 #>  2        1     0 S        adults     695 #>  3        1     0 I        children     5 #>  4        1     0 I        adults       5 #>  5        1     0 R        children     0 #>  6        1     0 R        adults       0 #>  7        2     0 S        children   295 #>  8        2     0 S        adults     695 #>  9        2     0 I        children     5 #> 10        2     0 I        adults       5 #> # ℹ 3,650 more rows  ggplot(sim_age, aes(time, value, colour = age,                     group = interaction(age, particle))) +   geom_line(alpha = 0.4) +   facet_wrap(~variable)

title: Tidy output from odin2, dust2 and monty
text: Fit SIR model case data particle filter, saving trajectories final state sample: model beta gamma strongly correlated posterior, random walk proposal given matching covariance (taken short pilot run) help chains mix: Parameters, chain iteration recorded trace plots:  fitted trajectories need filter , samples record names state variables times:
code: data <- data.frame(   time = 1:20,   cases = c(4, 8, 5, 12, 13, 19, 29, 34, 39, 42, 51, 44, 49, 38, 41, 33, 27,             21, 22, 13)) filter <- dust_filter_create(sir, time_start = 0, data = data,                              n_particles = 100, dt = 0.25) packer <- monty_packer(c("beta", "gamma"), fixed = list(N = 1000, I0 = 10)) likelihood <- dust_likelihood_monty(filter, packer, save_trajectories = TRUE,                                     save_state = TRUE) prior <- monty_dsl({   beta ~ Exponential(mean = 0.5)   gamma ~ Exponential(mean = 0.2) }) vcv <- matrix(c(0.051, 0.040, 0.040, 0.035), 2, 2) sampler <- monty_sampler_random_walk(vcv) samples <- monty_sample(likelihood + prior, sampler, 3000,                         initial = c(0.7, 0.45), n_chains = 3) #> ⡀⠀ Sampling [▁▁▁] ■                                |   0% ETA:  1m #> ⠄⠀ Sampling [▂▁▁] ■■■                              |   7% ETA:  9s #> ⢂⠀ Sampling [█▂▁] ■■■■■■■■■■■■■                    |  38% ETA:  6s #> ⡂⠀ Sampling [██▁] ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■           |  71% ETA:  3s #> ✔ Sampled 9000 steps across 3 chains in 9.3s #>  samples <- monty_samples_thin(samples, burnin = 1000, thinning_factor = 5) pars <- tidy_pars(samples) pars #> # A tibble: 2,400 × 5 #>    .chain .iteration .draw parameter value #>     <int>      <int> <int> <chr>     <dbl> #>  1      1          1     1 beta      0.675 #>  2      1          1     1 gamma     0.441 #>  3      1          2     2 beta      0.675 #>  4      1          2     2 gamma     0.441 #>  5      1          3     3 beta      1.08  #>  6      1          3     3 gamma     0.818 #>  7      1          4     4 beta      0.558 #>  8      1          4     4 gamma     0.348 #>  9      1          5     5 beta      0.558 #> 10      1          5     5 gamma     0.348 #> # ℹ 2,390 more rows  ggplot(pars, aes(.iteration, value, colour = factor(.chain))) +   geom_line() +   facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free_y") +   labs(colour = "chain") fit <- tidy_trajectories(samples, filter, vars = "incidence") fit #> # A tibble: 24,000 × 6 #>    .chain .iteration .draw  time variable  value #>     <int>      <int> <int> <int> <chr>     <dbl> #>  1      1          1     1     1 incidence     8 #>  2      1          1     1     2 incidence     7 #>  3      1          1     1     3 incidence     7 #>  4      1          1     1     4 incidence    13 #>  5      1          1     1     5 incidence    13 #>  6      1          1     1     6 incidence    19 #>  7      1          1     1     7 incidence    31 #>  8      1          1     1     8 incidence    40 #>  9      1          1     1     9 incidence    40 #> 10      1          1     1    10 incidence    37 #> # ℹ 23,990 more rows  ggplot(fit, aes(time, value)) +   geom_line(aes(group = .draw), alpha = 0.03) +   geom_point(aes(y = cases), data = data, colour = "red")

what: Running the model over many parameter sets
title: Tidy output from odin2, dust2 and monty
text: run_parameter_sets() runs model initial conditions, per parameter set, returns object structure samples. parameter sets can data frame one row per set. Parameters stay every set go fixed: structure matches fit, functions tidy . parameter set draw, parameters join trajectories .draw:  n_particles sets number stochastic realisations per parameter set. deterministic = TRUE stochastic model instead run per set using expectations place random draws:
code: grid <- data.frame(beta = c(0.2, 0.3, 0.5)) sweep <- run_parameter_sets(sir, grid, times = 0:60,                             fixed = list(gamma = 0.1, N = 1000),                             n_particles = 20, dt = 0.25) sweep #>  #> ── <monty_samples: 1 parameter x 3 samples x 1 chain> ────────────────────────── #> ℹ Parameters: 'beta' #> ℹ Conversion to other types is possible: #> → ! posterior::as_draws_array() [package installed, but not loaded] #> → ! posterior::as_draws_df() [package installed, but not loaded] #> → ✖ coda::as.mcmc.list() [package missing] #> ℹ These samples have associated observations #> ℹ See `?monty_sample()` and `vignette("samples")` for more information sweep_tidy <- dplyr::left_join(   tidy_trajectories(sweep, vars = "I"),   dplyr::select(tidy_pars(sweep), .draw, beta = value),   by = ".draw")  ggplot(sweep_tidy, aes(time, value, group = interaction(.draw, particle),                        colour = factor(beta))) +   geom_line(alpha = 0.4) +   labs(colour = "beta", y = "I") sweep_det <- run_parameter_sets(sir, grid, times = 0:60,                                 fixed = list(gamma = 0.1, N = 1000),                                 deterministic = TRUE, dt = 0.25)  ggplot(tidy_trajectories(sweep_det, vars = "I"),        aes(time, value, colour = factor(.draw))) +   geom_line() +   labs(colour = "parameter set", y = "I")

title: Tidy output from odin2, dust2 and monty
text: continue_parameter_sets() carries final state time set samples, sample continuing state using parameters. fit needs filter packer, likelihood must created save_state = TRUE. posterior draw projected forward 20 days:  result either function can continued, n_particles runs several realisations forward draw’s state.
code: projection <- continue_parameter_sets(samples, times = 20:40, obj = filter,                                       packer = packer)  both <- dplyr::bind_rows(   fit = fit,   projection = tidy_trajectories(projection, vars = "incidence"),   .id = "period")  ggplot(both, aes(time, value)) +   geom_line(aes(group = interaction(.draw, period), colour = period),             alpha = 0.03) +   geom_point(aes(y = cases), data = data) +   guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1)))

title: Tidy output from odin2, dust2 and monty
text: Posterior samples can also passed run_parameter_sets() rerun model start. modify changes parameter set run. Running baseline way gives like--like comparison, since unfiltered simulations:
code: baseline <- run_parameter_sets(sir, samples, times = 0:40, packer = packer,                                dt = 0.25) reduced <- run_parameter_sets(sir, samples, times = 0:40, packer = packer,                               modify = function(p) {                                 p$beta <- p$beta * 0.7                                 p                               }, dt = 0.25) scenarios <- dplyr::bind_rows(   baseline = tidy_trajectories(baseline, vars = "incidence"),   "30% lower transmission" = tidy_trajectories(reduced, vars = "incidence"),   .id = "scenario")  ggplot(summarise_trajectories(scenarios), aes(time, fill = scenario)) +   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.3) +   geom_line(aes(y = median, colour = scenario))

code: library(tidyodin) library(ggplot2)  # A stochastic SIR model sir <- odin2::odin({   update(S) <- S - n_SI   update(I) <- I + n_SI - n_IR   update(R) <- R + n_IR   p_SI <- 1 - exp(-beta * I / N * dt)   p_IR <- 1 - exp(-gamma * dt)   n_SI <- Binomial(S, p_SI)   n_IR <- Binomial(I, p_IR)   initial(S) <- N - I0   initial(I) <- I0   initial(R) <- 0   N <- parameter(1000)   I0 <- parameter(10)   beta <- parameter(0.4)   gamma <- parameter(0.1) })  # Run 30 particles and tidy the output sys <- dust2::dust_system_create(sir, list(), n_particles = 30, dt = 0.25) dust2::dust_system_set_state_initial(sys) t <- 0:60 y <- dust2::dust_system_simulate(sys, t)  ggplot(tidy_simulation(y, sys, t), aes(time, value, group = particle)) +   geom_line(alpha = 0.3) +   facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_y") +   theme_bw()
